newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end lower in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end lower in thin volume.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures closed mostly lower in lacklustre trade on Friday, with many market participants sidelined in the absence of new incentives and ahead of the G7 meeting this weekend, traders said on Friday.
"There's just no news," said one trader. "We're waiting to see how the dollar reacts to the G7 meeting over the weekend."

TOCOM aluminium ended 0.9 to 1.4 yen lower, with the newly listed benchmark April 1998 contract unchanged at 207.0 yen per kg. The day's estimated volume was 2,120 lots, the lowest since the contract was launched on April 7.

Traders said neither the dollar nor the LME provided any inspiration for Friday's trade. Aluminium retreated to $1,594 per tonne by the kerb close in London overnight, after hitting a high of $1,610, despite another 3,250-tonne LME stock decline.
